title: KO-04-C1 Commit-point crash matrix

events.label: run 1: save B, crash before_pointer_rename
events.detail: Store holds v1 = A. Save B and kill the writer just BEFORE the CURRENT rename (the commit point). Expected after recovery: A.

events.label: append BEGIN record -> journal.wal
events.detail: Write-ahead intent: the BEGIN record (old -> new version, SHA-256 of the new body, salted CRC) is appended to the journal BEFORE any data is written, so recovery can recognise this save if we die mid-way.

events.label: fsync journal.wal
events.detail: fsync makes the BEGIN record durable: from now on recovery will know this save was in flight.

events.label: create .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: Copy-on-write: v2 goes into a brand-new temp file created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL in the same directory. The current version is never modified in place.

events.label: write 132 B -> .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: The version frame (header + SHA-256 + body) is written. It sits only in the kernel page cache until fsync: dataDurable=false, a power cut could lose or tear it.

events.label: fsync .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: fsync BEFORE rename: the data must be on stable storage before any name points at it (the ext4 zero-length-file lesson, 2009). dataDurable turns true.

events.label: rename .v000002.dat.tmp -> v000002.dat
events.detail: rename(2) atomically gives the finished file its final name v000002.dat. It is NOT current: CURRENT still names the old version, so readers and recovery ignore it.

events.label: fsync dir report
events.detail: fsync(dir) makes the new name v000002.dat durable (PostgreSQL durable_rename lesson). The version is safely on disk but is NOT the current version yet.

events.label: create .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: The new one-line pointer is prepared in its own temp file (O_CREAT|O_EXCL), never by editing CURRENT in place.

events.label: write 91 B -> .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: Pointer text 'ADOC-CURRENT <format> <version> <sha256> <crc32>': self-validating, so a torn pointer can never be mistaken for a good one. Not durable yet.

events.label: fsync .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: The pointer bytes are flushed BEFORE the rename that will publish them.

events.label: CRASH at before_pointer_rename (kill -9)
events.detail: The process dies right here: no cleanup code, no more system calls. A process crash keeps the kernel page cache, so everything already written is still there - but whatever was not fsynced (dataDurable/entryDurable false) would not survive a power cut.

events.label: reopen store -> recovery runs
events.detail: Opening the store runs crash recovery first: truth = CURRENT if it parses and its target's SHA-256 verifies, otherwise the newest version that verifies.

events.label: read journal.wal (1 records, ok)
events.detail: Recovery scans the journal: 1 BEGIN without COMMIT = a save that was in flight. The journal is used for cleanup and reporting, never as the source of truth.

events.label: unlink .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: Recovery deletes a leftover temp file: only renames commit anything, so a .tmp was never committed by construction.

events.label: read CURRENT -> v1
events.detail: CURRENT parses and its CRC matches: it names v1.

events.label: read v000001.dat (SHA-256 ok)
events.detail: Header and SHA-256 verify: v000001.dat is a whole version.

events.label: unlink v000002.dat (roll back)
events.detail: Rollback: v2 is above the version recovery accepted, so it was never committed and is deleted. The committed version is untouched.

events.label: fsync v000001.dat
events.detail: Recovery flushes the file its decision rests on before checkpointing the journal, so a crash right after recovery finds exactly the same answer.

events.label: fsync CURRENT
events.detail: Recovery flushes the file its decision rests on before checkpointing the journal, so a crash right after recovery finds exactly the same answer.

events.label: fsync dir report
events.detail: Directory flush: the deletions and renames recovery made are now durable.

events.label: fsync dir docs
events.detail: Directory flush: the deletions and renames recovery made are now durable.

events.label: create journal.wal.tmp
events.detail: Checkpoint begins: a brand-new journal (fresh random salt) is built in a temp file.

events.label: rename journal.wal.tmp -> journal.wal
events.detail: Checkpoint: the fresh journal (new random salt) atomically replaces the old one; stale records can never validate again (the SQLite WAL salt idea).

events.label: fsync dir store
events.detail: Checkpoint durable: the fresh journal has replaced the old one. Recovery is complete.

events.label: decision: removed 1 leftover temp file(s)
events.detail: Temp files are never committed (only a rename commits), so deleting them is always safe.

events.label: decision: ROLLED BACK the in-flight save
events.detail: The journal shows BEGIN without COMMIT and CURRENT never named the new version, so it was never committed: its version file is deleted, the old version stays.

events.label: read CURRENT -> v1
events.detail: CURRENT parses and its CRC matches: it names v1.

events.label: read v000001.dat (SHA-256 ok)
events.detail: Header and SHA-256 verify: v000001.dat is a whole version.

events.label: run 1 (before_pointer_rename): recovered to A
events.detail: got A

events.label: run 1: no temp files, journal checkpointed
